To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the classes NP, P, and P/poly can be characterized by their self-reducibility and p-selectivity properties.

(1) p-selective self-reducible sets are in P; (2) p-selective sets are in P if and only if they are self-reducible; (3) there is a p-selective non-self-reducible NP set; and (4) there is a non-p-T-mitmotic NP set.
(a) any p-selective self-reducible set is in P; (b) any p-selectively self-reducible set that is also p-T-mitotic is in P; and (c) there exist non-p-T-mitic sets in NP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: what are the sets which can be computed in polynomial time?
the study of self-reducible sets.
the following question: What is the relationship between the class of p-selective self-reducible sets and the complexity class P?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is an interesting, but rather technical paper.
the class of P-selective self-reducible sets coincides with P, and this is a new characterization of this class.
the authors have shown that any p- selective and self-reducible set is in P and the converse is true as well.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new characterization of NP, namely that a set is in NP if and only if it is p-selective self-reducible.
we have shown the following: (1) P-selective self-reducible sets = P; (2) P-selective autoreducible sets = PSPACE; (3) NP contains non-p-T-mitto sets.
we have shown that the notion of self reducibility is a very strong notion and that it is not a trivial property to have a set that has it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the self-reducibility of a set is not a property of the set alone.
the class of sets with polynomially bounded self-reducibility properties (such as p-mitotic, p-reducibility and p-selectivity) is exactly the class P.
the class P is characterized by the property of being both p-selective and p-self-reducible.
